translation: Dear Mr., Mrs. Katz, We are in a fine hotel, but it's raining a lot. I'll be home Sunday. Hope the children wrote you. Regards to you and your husband, from me and husband.
notes: Spring Valley 1943 postcard to Mrs Katz 342 E 8th St NYC

translation: Yesterday, I have again received bad news from my brother Shmuel from Gura Humora that our dear mother has died on 16 December 1909. This is sad news to lose a mother and a brother in 30 days. I am beside myself and therefore I cannot write a lot because it's such a torture. Write to me and to our brother about Yekl's death. I must end this letter because my hand trembles from anguish over such a news. I send you my greetings and especially to your children. Regards to everyone from my wife and children. From me, your brother-in-law, J. Schapiro
Ofer Daian 1 year. As a memento to Uncle Sam.
notes: From Ofer Daian in Ashdot Yaacov to Uncle Sam and Aunt Lillian in USA. Hebrew script below English note.

translation: As an eternal memento I send my photo to my best and dearest Uncle and Aunt and Cousins. I am Naum Sheyndman with the mother Basha Shenderovich.

He greets the recipient. Aryeh son of Baila, should live. We received your card with two dollars. May God help you and your wife Fraida Esther, you shall be healthy and have luck and blessings. You should raise your children with nachas and ease and all good blessings. And you should have a blessed and good year. Yehoshua Heshil.
notes: Letter from Rabbis Mendil Friedman David Tversky, Buhusi Romania

translation: 4 Reeh [possibly Wednesday 31 August 1910]. My beloved friend, the groom, Eliyahu Tzvi Sudelnitzki. First, I can tell you about my health, I'm an old man of 75 years old. I have no more strength. But thank God that I am well. Second, I am writing you because you have written us in your letter after Pesach that you would be coming home this summer. Now, you have delayed your coming, we don't know what to do. You already know our misfortune, your mother has died, we are left behind forlorn. Write us what we should do with the house. Before Pesach I put flooring, it cost me 10 roubles. Now I made a basement, it cost me 7 roubles. The week Mameh died, I spent over 30 roubles. We intended to save her but it did not work out. Write me what is with you. Above all, if you intend to come home or not. And if you will already be an American citizen. For our sake, write us, we want to know what to do. We need to make the oven. We need to repair the roof. Write me what we should do. I want you to come home. Because I am already old. I barely walk around. If God want to give you luck, He will give you. May God give you a good inscription and a good seal for the New Year, amen. Avraham Dov Sudelnitzki
notes: 1910 letter from Avraham Dov Sudelnitzki to son in America

translation: This picture was taken in the station before Purim when Alter Zolerin was leaving. Departed happily.

translation: Received 20 February 1940 in Shanghai. My dears, A big thank you for your interest in us. I inform you that we are all well. And our entire family sends you their greetings. Also your mother, Manya and all the children are well. Yours, Helena.
notes: Shanghai 1940, red ink, Shanghai postal stamp 上海 20.2.29/9, received stamp FEB 20 1940. Jewish refugees in Shanghai during WWII.
